'''Sivaguru S. Sritharan''' (also known as '''S. S. Sritharan''') is an American [[aerodynamicist]] and [[mathematician]].<ref name=VC>{{Cite web|url=http://www.msruas.ac.in/organisation/vc|title=Vice Chancellor|access-date=July 19, 2020|work=[[Ramaiah University of Applied Sciences]]}}</ref>

Sritharan served in civilian universities such as [[University of Southern California]] and [[University of Wyoming]] as faculty member and head of the department and also in the Department of Defense ([[U. S. Navy]] and [[U. S. Air Force]]) in various capacities ranging from scientist to leadership roles, and also held visiting positions at several international institutions.<ref name=VC/>

He served as the [[vice chancellor]] at the [[Ramaiah University of Applied Sciences]] in [[Bengaluru]], [[India]].<ref name=VC/>

==Education==
Sritharan had his high schooling at [[Jaffna Central College]]. He then joined at [[University of Sri Lanka]] ([[Peradeniya]]) and obtained a BSc (Honors) degree in [[mechanical engineering]]. He obtained a Master of Science degree in [[aeronautics]] and [[astronautics]] from [[University of Washington]] and a master's degree and Ph.D. in [[applied mathematics]] from [[University of Arizona]].<ref name=CO>{{Cite web|url=https://contactout.com/SIVAGURUS-SRITHARAN-1059022|title=SIVAGURU S. SRITHARAN|access-date=July 19, 2020|work=ContactOut}}</ref><ref name=VC/>

==Career==
Sritharan served as the first [[Provost (education)|provost]] and vice chancellor of the [[Air Force Institute of Technology]] at [[Dayton, Ohio]] and as the dean of the Graduate School of Engineering and Applied Sciences at the [[Naval Postgraduate School]], [[Monterey, California]].<ref name=VC/>

He was a professor and head of the Department of Mathematics at [[University of Wyoming]] and head of the Science and Technology Branch at the [[Naval Information Warfare Systems Command]] in [[San Diego]].<ref name=VC/>

==Public engagements==
[[File:Sivaguru S. Sritharan at Port City Colombo.jpg|thumb|Sritharan, during a meeting with the leadership team of [[Port City Colombo]] at the site of the future Colombo International Financial Centre (CIFC) in June 2026.]]
In 2025, Sritharan served as Global Validation Chair of the [[Asian Digital Finance Forum & Awards]], held at [[Port City Colombo]] as part of the Asia International Digital Economy & AI in Finance Summit. In this capacity, he oversaw the independent validation process for recognising contributions to [[artificial intelligence]]–driven [[financial innovation]] across Asia.<ref>{{cite news |title=Dr. Sritharan appointed Global Validation Chair for Asian Digital Finance Awards 2025 |url=https://www.dailymirror.lk/business-news/Dr-Sritharan-appointed-Global-Validation-Chair-for-Asian-Digital-Finance-Awards-2025/273-316508
 |publisher=Daily Mirror |date=12 August 2025}}</ref>

He also delivered a keynote address at the forum examining the evolution of algorithmic finance and its convergence with advanced mathematics and artificial intelligence.<ref>{{cite news |title=Asian Digital Finance Forum & Awards 2025 convenes at Port City Colombo|url=https://www.ft.lk/financial-services/Asian-Digital-Finance-Forum-Awards-2025-convenes-at-Port-City-Colombo/42-783881|publisher=Daily FT |date=4 November 2025}}</ref>

==Contributions==
Sritharan is known for his research contributions in rigorous mathematical theory, [[optimal control]] and [[stochastic analysis]] of [[fluid mechanics]] and [[Magnetohydrodynamics|magneto-hydrodynamics]].<ref name=B1>{{Citation
 | last= Sritharan | first= S.S.
 | year= 2019
 | title= Invariant Manifold Theory for Hydrodynamic Transition
 | publisher= Courier Dover Publications
 | isbn= 9780486828282
 | url= https://books.google.com/books?id=ADiTtgEACAAJ
}}</ref><ref name=B2>{{Citation
 | last= Sritharan | first= S.S.
 | year= 1998
 | title= Optimal Control of Viscous Flow
 | publisher= SIAM
 | isbn= 9780898714067
 | url= https://books.google.com/books?id=uoBXMaeuuloC&q=Optimal+Control+of+Viscous+Flow
}}</ref>

His notable contributions include:

1. Developing [[dynamic programming]] method for the [[equations of fluid dynamics]]. This subject is closely related to reinforcement learning in the language of machine learning.<ref name=P1>{{Citation
 | last= Sritharan | first= S.S.
 | year= 1991
 | title= "Dynamic Programming of the Navier-Stokes Equations," in Systems and Control Letters, Vol. 16, No. 4, pp. 299-307
 | journal= Systems & Control Letters
 | volume= 16
 | issue= 4
 | pages= 299–307
 | publisher= [[Elsevier]]
 | doi= 10.1016/0167-6911(91)90020-F
 | url= https://dx.doi.org/10.1016/0167-6911%2891%2990020-F
|access-date=July 20, 2020| url-access= subscription
 }}</ref>

2. First complete proof of the [[Pontryagin's maximum principle|Pontryagin’s Maximum Principle]] for [[fluid dynamic]] equations with state constraints, as a joint work with [[UCLA]] mathematician [[Hector. O. Fattorini]].<ref name=P2>{{Citation
 | last1=Fattorini| first1=H. O.
 | last2=Sritharan | first2= S.S.
 | year= 1994
 | title=  "Necessary and Sufficient Conditions for Optimal Controls in Viscous Flow," Proceedings of the Royal Society of Edinburgh, Series A, Vol. 124A, pp. 211-251
 | journal=Proceedings of the Royal Society of Edinburgh Section A: Mathematics
 | volume=124
 | issue=2
 | pages=211–251
 | publisher= [[Proceedings of the Royal Society]]
 | doi=10.1017/S0308210500028444
 | s2cid=18018847
 | url= https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/proceedings-of-the-royal-society-of-edinburgh-section-a-mathematics/article/necessary-and-sufficient-conditions-for-optimal-controls-in-viscous-flow-problems/60E9D5113DD26331EFE288201EB4BBA4
|access-date=July 20, 2020| url-access=subscription
 }}</ref>

3. Developing robust [[H-infinity methods in control theory|(H-infinity) control theory]] for fluid dynamics as a joint work with Romanian mathematician [[Viorel P. Barbu]].<ref name=P3>{{Citation
 | last1=Barbu| first1= V. 
 | last2=Sritharan | first2= S.S.
 | year= 1998
 | title= "H-infinity-control theory of fluid dynamics," Proceedings of The Royal Society of London, Series A, pp. 3009-3033, Vol. 356, No. 1979, November 1998
 | publisher= [[Proceedings of the Royal Society]]
 | url= https://www.afit.edu/BIOS/docs/R19.pdf
|access-date=July 20, 2020}}</ref>

4. First successful rigorous theory establishing a direct [[stochastic]] analogy to the famous [[Jacques-Louis Lions]] and G. Prodi (1959) on existence and uniqueness theorem for the two dimensional [[Navier-Stokes equation]] as a joint work with [[J. L. Menaldi]] utilizing a subtle local [[monotonicity]] property.<ref name=P4>{{Citation
 | last1=Menaldi| first1= J. L. 
 | last2=Sritharan | first2= S.S.
 | year= 2002
 | title= "Stochastic 2-D Navier-Stokes equation," Applied Mathematics and Optimization, 46, 2002, pp. 31-53
 | publisher= [[Wayne State University]]
 | url= https://digitalcommons.wayne.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1083&context=mathfrp
|access-date=July 20, 2020}}</ref>

5. Proving Large Deviation Principle for stochastic Navier-Stokes equation as a joint work with [[Padmanabhan Sundar|P. Sundar]] to estimate the probability of rare events.<ref name=P5>{{Citation
 | last1= Sundar| first1= P. 
 | last2=Sritharan | first2= S.S.
 | year= 2006
 | title= "Large Deviations for Two-dimensional Stochastic Navier-Stokes Equations", Stochastic Processes, Theory and Applications, Vol. 116, Issue 11, (2006), 1636-1659
 | publisher= [[Elsevier]]
 | url= https://www.afit.edu/BIOS/docs/R37.pdf
|access-date=July 20, 2020}}</ref>

6. Systematic development of differential geometric methods for aerodynamics of supersonic delta wings.<ref>{{cite journal
 | last1 = Sritharan
 | first1 = S. S.
 | last2 = Seebass
 | first2 = A. R.
 | title = A Finite Area Method for Nonlinear Supersonic Conical Flows
 | journal = AIAA Journal
 | volume = 22
 | issue = 2
 | date = February 1984
 | pages = 226–233
 | publisher = [[American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics]]
 | url=https://arc.aiaa.org/doi/10.2514/3.8372
}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal
 | last = Sritharan
 | first = S. S.
 | title = Delta Wings with Shock-Free Cross Flow
 | journal = Quarterly of Applied Mathematics
 | date = October 1985
 | pages = 275–286
 | publisher = [[Brown University]]
 | url= https://www.afit.edu/BIOS/docs/R2.pdf
}}</ref>

7. Advancing geometric theory of hydrodynamic transition to turbulence.<ref>{{cite book
 | last = Sritharan
 | first = S. S.
 | title = Invariant Manifold Theory for Hydrodynamic Transition
 | publisher = [[John Wiley & Sons]] (Reprinted as part of the Dover Mathematics Classics series by [[Dover Publications]], January 2019)
 | year = 1990
 | isbn = 
 | edition = Monograph
 | url= https://store.doverpublications.com/products/9780486836867?srsltid=AfmBOopC8Z1KJ_hQLhVPXtMwdBppvipt4m5fFFRbWue5s5nCz-HsDxXW
}}</ref>

8. Developing nonlinear filtering theory for stochastic Navier-Stokes equations for the estimation of turbulence based on partial measurements and similar theories for models describing quantum dynamics.<ref>{{cite book
 | last = Sritharan
 | first = S. S.
 | title = Nonlinear Filtering of Stochastic Navier–Stokes Equations

 | year = 1996
